title: Revives the dead (Berakhot 58b)
hook: seeing a friend after a year, one blesses the One who revives the dead
tomorrow: is there a blessing just for opening your eyes in the morning?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ready for me: Ben Zoma woke to bread a long line of people made, and said all this was done for me, like a good guest. Today the week comes back, with one more blessing.
screen: `ALL THIS WAS DONE FOR ME.` → `THE WEEK COMES BACK.`

segments.voice: At an airport arrivals gate, somebody always screams. A year apart, and then a face comes around the corner, and nobody says anything sensible. So what do you say to a friend you haven't seen in a year? The Talmud has the words. Blessed is the One who revives the dead. It sounds like too much, until you hear why.
screen: `THE ARRIVALS GATE.` → `A YEAR APART.` → `WHO REVIVES THE DEAD.`

segments.voice: Here's the rule. See a friend after thirty days, and you bless God who has kept us alive and brought us to this time. After twelve months, you say: who revives the dead. Rav explains the year. The dead are forgotten from the heart only after twelve months, and he reads a psalm about being forgotten like the dead, out of mind. A year is long enough for someone to slip out of the everyday heart. Seeing them again isn't only nice. It's a small return from the forgotten, so it gets the words that the Amidah uses for God who gives life. Now look back at the week. Rava sent a man to bless the place of his rescue. The Mishnah said bless for the bad too, with both inclinations. A dream was a letter unread. A sound, a sight and a smell restored a person. A crowd held every mind different. And Ben Zoma found it all ready for him. Every one of these is the same move: notice the ordinary thing, and give it its blessing.
screen: `THIRTY DAYS: KEPT US ALIVE.` · `TWELVE MONTHS: REVIVES THE DEAD.` · `FORGOTTEN FROM THE HEART.` · `A WEEK OF BLESSING THE ORDINARY.` · then, large: `REVIVES THE DEAD.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one friend you haven't seen in a long time. Let their face come back: the voice, the laugh, the way they stood. Notice how much of them was still there, waiting, and hold that for the rest of the sit.
screen: `ONE FRIEND, LONG UNSEEN.` · `THE FACE COMES BACK.` · `STILL THERE.`

segments.voice: Revives the dead: the Talmud's blessing for a friend seen after a year, someone almost forgotten from the heart, returned.
For the next long-awaited hug: revives the dead, said with a laugh if you like. Thirty-nine down, eleven to go.

howItsDone: Jewish law gives a blessing on seeing a dear friend after thirty days (shehecheyanu) and after twelve months (mechayeh ha-metim, who revives the dead); the same phrase praises God in the Amidah.
